intent.statement: Replace AI-assisted cleanup with the lossless-preserved-text block selection algorithm defined in 0_Planning/AI_Cleanup_Lossless_Block_Replacement_Plan.md.

examples: A blank-line gap between a story block and a separator is accepted and recorded; a changed character, reordered block, or unexplained non-whitespace gap rejects the window.
spec_items.statement: Every preserved AI Cleanup block must match an exact non-overlapping forward slice of the window's single canonical source string. Whitespace-only gaps may be normalized deterministically and recorded; any gap containing non-whitespace source requires an intervening high-confidence removable decision.

examples: Dialogue and narration are story; a high-confidence header may authorize removal; a medium-confidence noise block remains.
spec_items.statement: artifact_type is exactly header, footer, noise, separator, heading, or story. High-confidence header, footer, and noise are removed; separator, heading, and story plus every medium/low-confidence block are preserved. No action field is used.

examples: A response containing schema_version, action, page identity, unresolved placeholders, duplicate source, a wrong window_id, or a skipped block ID is rejected.
spec_items.statement: Cleanup prompts use only text_cleanup_system and text_cleanup_user, contain the concatenated once-canonicalized source exactly once inside resolved window markers, and responses contain exactly window_id plus ordered text_blocks whose items contain text_block_id, text_block, artifact_type, and confidence. There is no schema_version, action, page, or segment field.

examples: Fixtures evaluate 1.5, 1.75, and 2.0 expansion policies; the production default is 2.0 and an impossible single segment fails preflight.
spec_items.statement: The window builder targets four consecutive pages and reserves input plus worst-case escaped preserved-text JSON output using a configurable expansion factor defaulting to 2.0, shrinking or safely segmenting before provider submission when required.

examples: Legacy response, prompt, taxonomy, checkpoint, and public-entry-point compatibility is unsupported; incompatible state restarts at window one.
spec_items.statement: AI Cleanup checkpoints only fully validated current-contract windows, uses an internal contract fingerprint to reject obsolete state without interpreting it, restarts changed-input checkpoints, resumes changed profiles only at the next untouched window, and persists complete review artifacts and model history.
